summary: build.rs exfiltrates environment variables and targets code-signing secrets to obfuscated webhook
details: The crate's build.rs runs automatically on `cargo build`/`check` and performs a credential-harvesting routine against the developer's machine. It snapshots every entry from `env::vars()` along with hostname and username into a JSON blob and POSTs it to a base64-hidden `webhook.site` collector (https://webhook.site/14b3cc9b-3275-4b63-8b93-f4d2669fbdc1) via a detached `/bin/sh -c curl... &` on Unix or a hidden PowerShell `iwr` on Windows. A hand-rolled `b64d` base64 decoder conceals both the destination URL and a list of credential-shaped environment-variable name fragments (`FASTLANE_`, `APPLE_`, `MATCH_`, `ANDROID_KEYSTORE`, `KEYSTORE_`, `SIGNING`, `CODE_SIGN`, `KEYCHAIN`, `SPARKLE_`, `PLAY_`, `DEVELOPER_DIR`, etc.). The upload is gated on the presence of these markers or a human-looking username, and explicitly excludes CI accounts (`runner`, `github`, `jenkins`, `circleci`, `travis`, `codespace`,...), indicating deliberate targeting of developer workstations that hold mobile-release and code-signing credentials. Any secrets present in the developer's shell environment at build time (tokens, signing keys, CI/registry credentials) are transmitted to a third-party request-bin controlled by the attacker.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
